findings.title: Non-default method added to public grant type SPI
findings.body: Adding `String getShortcut()` to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface without a default implementation is a binary/source incompatible change for existing third-party grant type providers. During `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, every `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is fetched and `getShortcut()` is invoked. Existing extension JARs compiled against the old interface will throw `AbstractMethodError` and can prevent server startup. A default implementation, separate capability interface, or migration/validation path is needed.

findings.title: Removed public Context copy constructor breaks extensions
findings.body: The public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context)` copy constructor was silently removed. External grant type implementations or other code using `new Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile and previously compiled binaries will fail with `NoSuchMethodError`. If this SPI is meant to be extensible, retaining the copy constructor or explicitly documenting the break is necessary.

findings.title: Wrong argument is null-checked for rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor validates `grantType` twice: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. `rawTokenId` is never checked and can be null, contrary to the constructor's apparent contract. A null raw ID is then accepted and can produce an encoded token ID with the string "null" as the identifier suffix.

findings.title: Encoder assumes exactly two-character grant type shortcuts
findings.body: The SPI contract for `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not require a two-character value, and its Javadoc even says shortcuts are usually like three letters. However, `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the encoded prefix to be exactly length 6 and splits it into fixed 2-character chunks, while `encodeTokenId()` performs no length validation. A custom grant type with a three-character shortcut will emit a longer prefix, and decoding that token ID will throw `IllegalArgumentException` because `encodedContext.length() != 6`, making valid providers unusable.

findings.title: Reserved UNKNOWN shortcut can silently mask a custom grant type
findings.body: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN` is the string "na", but it is inserted into `grantsByShortcuts` after all provider shortcuts and overwrites any provider using the same shortcut. The duplicate-shortcut validation only compares map sizes; for a grant whose shortcut is "na", the overwrite plus the added UNKNOWN entry can keep both map sizes equal and bypass validation. Such a grant would encode as "na" but decode as UNKNOWN, losing the grant type information.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses inverted condition and wrong substring
findings.body: The matcher extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)` rather than the grant-type range at indices 4-5, and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut instead of returning false when it does not. With the built-in shortcuts this means the condition is essentially never true, so any six-character prefix followed by a UUID passes. The test does not actually verify the grant type encoded in the token ID. It should likely be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
